text:
maria: heads-up — saw 3 small OOM spikes on prod-rlu-3 during the 09:10 traffic bump. root cause looks like continuous-batcher forming a single giant batch that exhausts KV cache headroom when long-context requests land together.

maria: profiling dump attached in the infra job — KV footprint grew ~2.6x per-batch compared to baseline. kernel switch to the new fused-attn path also increased transient memory by ~12%.

tom: can you paste the profiler snippet? wondering if it's prefork or post-kernel selection

maria: snippet:
```
batch_size=42
avg_req_tokens=1200
avg_kv_bytes_per_req=54MB
estimated_batch_kv=42 * 54MB = 2268MB
kv_capacity_headroom=1.5GB
oom_margin=-768MB
kernel_route=fused_attn_v2
```

siva: yikes — batch admission didn't account for per-request KV usage. current admission checks only token_budget and per-device free mem, not kv-reserved bytes.

jen: we saw similar pattern in canary last month but it was masked by prefetch caps. I think two things: add kv-aware admission and a timebox to avoid huge long-context coalescing.

maria: proposed heuristics:
- estimate per-request kv footprint at admission using recent avg_kv_bytes (fall back to cost model for unseen models)
- per-queue token_watermark + kv_headroom check: if estimated_batch_kv > device_kv_threshold, deny admit and requeue with short backoff
- timebox windows: cap max aggregation window to 6ms for tail-sensitive queues
- kernel fallback: prefer memory-frugal kernel (attn_v1_int8) when kv headroom low

tom: +1. also add an eviction-tolerant fallback: when admission would OOM, try trimming oldest KV entries in the batch (soft-eviction) before rejecting.

siva: trimming inside a forming batch is tricky but doable if we have deterministic prefix retention. Another idea: per-request kv_priority flag — short requests set low KV retention so they don't hold cache.

jen: ops concern — we need observability metrics for the heuristic: admitted_count, rejected_by_kv, avg_estimated_kv_per_batch, kernel_route_switches. Also should surface per-model kv coefficients in the console.

maria: experiment plan:
1) implement kv_estimate in admission path (feature flag: kv_admit_v1)
2) add kernel_fallback policy with switch threshold (feature flag: kernel_mem_guard)
3) metric plumbing and a canary on prod-rlu-3 with 1% traffic
4) run 48h soak, compare OOMs, p99 latency, avg tokens/second

tom: how to reproduce locally? can we script a synthetic load that coalesces long-context arrivals?

maria: repro command (local dev cluster):
```
./tools/loadgen --model redwood-xl --concurrency 60 \
  --seq-lens "1200:0.7,64:0.3" --arrival_poisson 8ms --tag kv-pressure-test
```

siva: note: kernel selection regression earlier was because fused_attn_v2 assumed smaller KV per token. adding kv-admit will show that v2 is fine for short-context but we should bias towards v1 when avg_kv_per_token > X.

jen: also add a continuous histogram of batch_estimated_kv so we can threshold empirically instead of hardcoding numbers.

ops-bot: deploy queued: feature/kv-admit-v1 -> staging (build #4512). Status: started.

maria: leaving TODOs: (1) implement kv_estimate model mapping (2) add metric names + dashboards (3) implement kernel_fallback policy (4) small e2e loadgen job and alert if rejected_by_kv > 0.5% during canary.

tom: I'll own (3) kernel_fallback; will add a quick scripted fallback that flips route to attn_v1_int8 and tracks perf delta.

siva: I'll add the kv_estimate model and the per-queue timebox.

jen: I'll add dashboard tiles and the canary watchbook entry.

maria: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 11:30 to review initial numbers. :thumbsup:

tom: sounds good. if we see regressions after fallback we can tune the kernel threshold. prefer iterative small changes to avoid broad perf regressions.

siva: one more thought: should we try adding a soft quota that reduces batching weight for heavy-kv requests instead of outright rejecting? could help latency.

maria: agree — add soft_shedding experiment flag after kv_admit_v1 lands.

jen: noted. will add to the canary checklist.

ops-bot: staging deploy complete. link: https://staging.redwood/infrastructure/deploys/4512

maria: good progress — will paste initial canary metrics in this thread once available.
